title: TRANSPOSE: Circuit Transformations for Power Side-Channel Security at Register Transfer Level
problem: Power side-channel attacks (PSCAs) on cryptographic hardware can leak secrets by passively probing overall device power consumption. Correlation between secret data and power consumption enables attackers to recover cryptographic keys.
motivation: Automated, synthesizable countermeasures at RTL enable practical deployment of power side-channel hardening without extensive manual effort or post-synthesis optimization.
method: The method automatically transforms circuit designs at the register-transfer level (RTL—the design stage before physical hardware is built) by combining three techniques: duplicating circuit components that process secrets, balancing register operations to equalize timing patterns, and using clock gating (selectively disabling clocks to hide active elements). These transformations randomize the power consumption so it no longer correlates with secret data, defeating power-based attacks on cryptographic keys. The hardened design is validated with TVLA (Test Vector Leakage Assessment), which verifies that power consumption no longer leaks information.
key_novelty: The core innovation is an automated RTL-level technique combining register duplication, balancing, and clock gating to randomize power consumption and reduce dynamic power draw, preventing power side-channel attacks on cryptographic hardware.
contributions: Automated PSCA countermeasure framework at RTL
Register duplication algorithm for sensitive data paths
TVLA validation on PRESENT and AES S-boxes
limitations: Abstract only; specific TVLA leakage reduction metrics not quantified; overhead (area, power, timing) not provided; limited evaluation to two ciphers.
primary_theme: Hardware security and side-channel attack mitigation
